attribution.note: The words are Marcus's own, from a footnote in his post. He frames the elephant example as coming from someone else, but the claim that the systems do not reliably deliver is his own assertion.

semantics.note: This is a firm present-tense observation ('They don't'). It keeps his concession about clever prompters. The narrowing to LLMs is acceptable but slightly loose, because the examples are image generation through ChatGPT/DALL-E. The contract flags that scope shift.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: recurring failures on simple requests without elaborate prompting, not that every request fails. A Feb 1–8, 2024 window is a reasonable anchor. With no threshold or task distribution named, the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: IFEval tests GPT-4 text instruction following using responses scraped in Nov 2023. That is a different period and a different modality from the image-generation examples, so it is context only.
This study shows DALL-E 3 negation prompts failing often, with only 12.3% agreement on unmodified prompts. Testing ran March–November 2024, outside the target period, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: Neither evidence item covers the Feb 1–8, 2024 target period: one tests text in Nov 2023, the other images in Mar–Nov 2024. Both point to recurring failures, but by the period rule they are context only. The packet has no independent repeated tests from the target period, and possible contemporaneous replications could not be read. The evidence therefore does not settle the claim.
